messages:
jessica: heads-up — found an .env with AWS creds in internal-plugins repo (plugins/payment/.env). It looks like a plaintext commit in history.
ops-bot: secret-scanner: high confidence AWS access key exposure in plugins/payment/.env (commit 9f3a2). https://scans.internal/alert/9932 :rotating_light:
mike: noted. @sanjay can you take lead on rotation + cleanup? we need revoke, rotate, and check CloudTrail for any usage.
sanjay: taking this. steps I'll run: create replacement creds, add to Vault, update CI, revoke old keys, then monitor. ETA ~45m.
claire: quick note — that key had permission s3:ListBucket on partner-account (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/partner-access). opening support ticket and adding block on cross-account principal.
jessica: question: creds were plaintext; do we need to rewrap any KMS envelope keys? the repo had backups encrypted under our CMK.
mike: for IAM creds you revoke/rotate — no rewrap needed. rewrap only matters for data encrypted under a CMK (S3 objects). check which S3 objects used CMK-id: cmk-1234abcd.
sanjay: rotation plan: 1) create IAM replacement key 2) push to Vault kv-v2 at secret/plugins/payment 3) update GH Actions to pull from Vault 4) revoke old key 5) run CloudTrail query for last 24h and export hits 6) open incident ticket + postmortem.
claire: long-term: prefer ephemeral roles (OIDC assume-role) for CI instead of long-lived IAM keys. short-term rotate to new key and then migrate.
jessica: agreed. also need to check Vault auto-unseal CMK policies — ensure not too permissive. add an audit event for the rotation.
cloudtrail-bot: cloudtrail: detected S3 GETs from exposed key at 2025-11-04T18:22:10Z to bucket partner-backups; 3 objects read. https://cloudtrail.internal/events/abc123
sanjay: that's bad. revoking now.
sanjay: ```
aws iam delete-access-key --user-name plugin-bot --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE123
```
claire: opened AWS support ticket #987654. also added an explicit deny policy to prevent plugin-bot from assuming partner-account role (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root).
jessica: repo hygiene question — we have plaintext in git history. should we rewrite history (BFG) to remove the secret or just rotate and keep history? legal/compliance input?
mike: we should rewrite history for internal repo to remove secrets. use BFG, coordinate with teams to rebase, preserve commit SHAs in an audit artifact. hold merges to that repo until sanitized.
sanjay: rotating and sanitizing now. will push sanitized commit and update CI secrets to Vault path. ETA ~1.5h for full cleanup + verify.
jessica: :thumbsup: paste ticket numbers and audit slices when done.
deploy-bot: CI-runner: disabled runners for plugins/payment (reason: secrets rotation) :no_entry_sign:
claire: RBAC change proposal: only CODEOWNERS/maintainers can push to plugins/* — I'll open a PR to enforce at org level.
mike: also enable S3 object-level access logging and export CloudTrail to secure bucket encrypted with CMK-rot1.
sanjay: update: rotated keys, created Vault entry at secret/plugins/payment (kv-v2), updated GH Actions to fetch from Vault, revoked old key at 2025-11-04T18:35Z. monitoring started.
jessica: please add a short incident timeline to the ticket and tag secops + compliance.
sanjay: done. ticket INC-2025-4111 created with timeline, logs attached. I'll write a postmortem within 72h.
mike: follow-ups after postmortem: 1) migrate all internal plugins to OIDC/assume-role or Vault AWS auth 2) enable pre-merge secret scanning that blocks commits with .env containing AWS keys 3) enforce repo history scrub for exposed secrets.
jessica: I'll own pre-merge scanning rollout. assigning Claire for RBAC PR and Sanjay for rotation + postmortem. we'll close thread after 48h watch.
monitoring-bot: started 48h CloudTrail monitor for keys related to plugin-bot; will alert #incidents on suspicious activity.
claire: ✅ RBAC PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/internal-plugins/pull/42
sanjay: ✅ rotation complete. ticket INC-2025-4111. logs: https://incidents.internal/INC-2025-4111/logs
mike: :lock: marking this thread resolved pending 48h monitoring window.
jessica: thanks everyone, please follow up on postmortem and remediation items.
